author: opencode-worker-3
text: ROUND 4 — replay.c semantics fully mapped: lichen_replay_check on a FRESH window (initialised=false) initialises to (epoch,seq,bitmap=1) and ACCEPTS; EALREADY is returned only for (a) seq==last_seq, (b) seq inside the 32-bit window already seen, (c) epoch < window epoch. Therefore the observed EALREADY on (142, seq0) and (142, seq1) — frames whose next_tx allocation is logged at the SAME timestamps (.350/1.250) — means each frame was COMMITTED ONCE ALREADY before the logged attempt: the frame IS processed twice through the commit path (first silent OK, second EALREADY), OR two different rx_ctx/table instances are in play. Ruled out this round: peer_try_all_pubkeys is SIID-indexed single-call (lichen_l2_peer.c:231, one lichen_link_rx per frame); lichen_link_rx calls commit_replay exactly once (:370); the driver delivers once per queue entry; lora_l2_rx ISR drop-on-busy prevents double-staging. NEXT (one instrumented run): DIAG at lichen_l2_input ENTRY (frame[0..3] hex + len) and at commit SUCCESS — count input invocations per frame: if input fires twice per frame, the duplication is between the driver cb and input (lora_l2 work/stage layer); if input fires once but commit runs twice, it is inside peer_try/link_rx (e.g. a second commit_replay call site or relay path). Also capture whether the FIRST (silent) commit is followed by successful stack injection (the udp observer timeout may then be a separate socket-path issue — the EALREADY log may be purely the duplicate's noise).
